pages.title: Page 1: Welcome and Purpose
pages.content:
Welcome and Purpose

Welcome to {{COURSE_NAME}}.

This guided introduction supports {{LANGUAGE_NAME}} writing fluency through structured keyboard practice in Moodle.

The audience for this course is {{AUDIENCE}}.

The current lesson focus is {{LESSON_FOCUS}}.

{{PILOT_GOAL}}

pages.title: Page 2: Why Keyboard Practice Matters for Language Learning
pages.content:
Why Keyboard Practice Matters

Typing reinforces recognition, recall, and production.

  1. Visual pattern recognition in {{LANGUAGE_NAME}} script.
  2. Motor memory linked to writing.
  3. Confidence in written output.
  4. Accuracy gains from immediate feedback.

Keyboard layout used in this course: {{KEYBOARD_LAYOUT}}.

pages.title: Page 3: Getting Started in This Course
pages.content:
Getting Started

  1. Open orientation and keyboard notes.
  2. Complete one short warm-up activity.
  3. Start Lesson 1 and retry at least once.

Best early habit: short, frequent practice with immediate repeats.

{{READINESS_CHECK_BLOCK}}

pages.title: Page 4: The Keyboard Layout
pages.content:
The Keyboard Layout

This course uses {{KEYBOARD_LAYOUT}} so students can type directly in the target script.

  1. Spend time orienting to key positions.
  2. Use early activities for familiarization.
  3. Build consistency before speed.

{{KEYBOARD_NOTES}}

pages.title: Page 5: How MooTyper Activities Work
pages.content:
How MooTyper Works

  1. Students type prompted text.
  2. They receive immediate feedback.
  3. Attempts can be repeated.
  4. Results can feed Moodle gradebook.

Cycle: attempt, review, repeat, improve.

{{LEARNING_INTENT_CHECK_BLOCK}}

pages.title: Page 6: Suggested Learning Path (Beginner to Advanced)
pages.content:
Suggested Learning Path

  1. Keyboard orientation.
  2. Beginner symbol and word patterns.
  3. Vocabulary reinforcement.
  4. Intermediate mixed review.
  5. Phrase-level typing.
  6. Applied fluency practice.

{{LEARNING_PATH_NOTES}}

pages.title: Page 7: For Teachers: Setup, Monitoring, and Feedback
pages.content:
For Teachers

  1. Assign structured typing practice.
  2. Monitor completion and performance.
  3. Identify students who need support.
  4. Use repeated attempts to track growth.

{{TEACHER_NOTES}}
